{{Short description|2x2 matrix with 1 and -1 coefficients}}
In [[mathematics]], the [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]]

: <math>\begin{pmatrix}
  1 & -1 \\
  1 & 1 
\end{pmatrix}</math>

is sometimes called the '''quincunx matrix'''. It is a 2&times;2 [[Hadamard matrix]], and its rows form the basis of a diagonal [[square lattice]] consisting of the integer points whose coordinates both have the same [[parity (mathematics)|parity]]; this lattice is a two-dimensional analogue of the three-dimensional [[cubic crystal system|body-centered cubic lattice]].<ref>{{citation|title=On the multidimensional extension of the quincunx subsampling matrix|last1= Van De Ville|first1= D.  |last2= Blu|first2= T. |last3=Unser|first3= M.|journal=IEEE Signal Processing Letters|volume=12|issue=2|year=2005|pages=112–115|doi=10.1109/LSP.2004.839697|bibcode= 2005ISPL...12..112V|url=http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~tblu/monsite/pdfs/vandeville0501.pdf|citeseerx= 10.1.1.649.9329}}.</ref>
